decisions.reason: It builds directly on the firm's core airfield lighting and control expertise, so with strong in-house R&D and integration capabilities the firm is likely to retain and refine it rather than withdraw it.

An air situation display fits the firm's established surveillance and airport-operations knowledge base, giving management enough related expertise to learn from early market feedback and improve the product commercially.
The training program complements the firm's installed systems and service business, and because it leverages existing operational know-how it is relatively easy for the firm to sustain and adapt.

This course is close to the firm's established airfield ground-lighting competence, but as a narrower training offer with weaker market visibility it faces a somewhat higher chance of being folded into broader services rather than fully discontinued.

Airport collaboration software strongly matches the firm's strategic move toward integrated, data-driven and collaborative airport operations, so absorptive capacity around systems integration supports continued commitment.

As a flagship surveillance product built on the firm's core airport technology base and backed by its R&D resources, management would be very likely to keep it on the market and continue developing it.
